concepts.title: Principal Value Branch of Inverse Sine Function
concepts.definition: The bijective restriction of the sine function onto a closed half-pi interval yields an inverse function whose standard output range is restricted between negative ninety degrees and positive ninety degrees.
concepts.key_idea: Domain is [-1, 1] and the principal range is [-pi/2, pi/2].

concepts.title: Principal Value Branch of Inverse Cosine Function
concepts.definition: Restricting the domain of cosine to the non-negative interval from zero to pi makes it invertible, producing a primary branch spanning zero to pi radians.
concepts.key_idea: Domain is [-1, 1] and the principal range is [0, pi].
question_patterns: find the principal value branch of inverse cosine

solution_steps.explain: verify that theta is the only angle in [0, pi] satisfying cos(theta) = x, which guarantees a well-defined principal value.

concepts.title: Principal Value Branch of Inverse Tangent Function
concepts.definition: The inverse tangent function maps the entire real line onto an open angular interval strictly between negative and positive half-pi.
concepts.key_idea: Domain is all real numbers and principal range is open interval (-pi/2, pi/2).
question_patterns: what is the domain and range of tan_inv

concepts.title: Principal Value Branch of Inverse Cotangent Function
concepts.definition: Inverse cotangent is defined for all real numbers with its principal value branch mapped into the open interval bounded by zero and pi radians.
concepts.key_idea: Domain is all real numbers and principal range is open interval (0, pi).

concepts.title: Principal Value Branches of Secant and Cosecant Functions
concepts.definition: Inverse secant and inverse cosecant map real values outside the unit open interval (-1, 1) to restricted angular branches excluding points where the base functions are undefined.
concepts.key_idea: Domains are R - (-1, 1) with ranges excluding pi/2 for sec_inv and 0 for cosec_inv.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find the principal value of sin_inv(1 / sqrt(2))

solution_template.explain: let y = sin_inv(1/sqrt(2)), which implies sin(y) = 1/sqrt(2)
sin(pi/4) = 1/sqrt(2) and pi/4 lies in [-pi/2, pi/2], so principal value is pi/4

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find the principal value of cot_inv(-1 / sqrt(3))

solution_template.explain: let y = cot_inv(-1/sqrt(3)), which gives cot(y) = -1/sqrt(3)
cot(y) = -cot(pi/3) = cot(pi - pi/3) = cot(2*pi/3); since 2*pi/3 is in (0, pi), principal value is 2*pi/3

worked_examples.question_pattern: Show that sin_inv(2*x*sqrt(1 - x^2)) = 2*sin_inv(x) for -1/sqrt(2) <= x <= 1/sqrt(2)

solution_template.explain: let x = sin(theta) so theta = sin_inv(x)

worked_examples.question_pattern: Express tan_inv(cos(x) / (1 - sin(x))) in simplest form

solution_template.explain: rewrite cos(x) as cos^2(x/2) - sin^2(x/2) and 1 - sin(x) as (cos(x/2) - sin(x/2))^2
cancel common factor (cos(x/2) - sin(x/2)) to get (cos(x/2) + sin(x/2)) / (cos(x/2) - sin(x/2)) = tan(pi/4 + x/2)

worked_examples.question_pattern: Write cot_inv(1 / sqrt(x^2 - 1)) for x > 1 in simplest form

solution_template.explain: let x = sec(theta) so sqrt(x^2 - 1) = tan(theta)
